title: Image-guided liver biopsy
description: Image-guided liver biopsy is a procedure where your doctor takes a small sample of liver tissue using a needle guided by ultrasound or CT imaging. This test helps your doctor diagnose liver diseases by examining liver tissue under a microscope. Your doctor will use imaging to guide a biopsy needle to the right spot in your liver while you remain awake. You'll receive local anesthesia to numb the area where the needle enters your skin. The biopsy needle removes a tiny piece of liver tissue that's sent to a lab for analysis. The procedure usually takes 15-30 minutes and generally causes minimal discomfort. After the procedure, you'll rest briefly and receive instructions about limiting activity for a few days while the biopsy site heals.
